name: Long mirrored stretches
brief:
A radio log records call signs as one string `tape` of lower-case letters. An analyst looks for stretches that read the same forwards and backwards, but short ones are noise.

Write `long_mirrors(tape, k)`, which returns how many stretches of `tape` with length at least `k` read the same both ways. A stretch is a run of neighbouring letters, and stretches at different positions count separately even when their letters agree.

Example. In `'abaab'` the stretches of length at least 2 that read the same both ways are `'aba'`, `'aa'` and `'baab'`, so for `k = 2` the answer is 3.
constraints: $1 \le n \le 300$ letters and $1 \le k \le 1{,}000$; `k` may be longer than the tape.
All the tests in a run share one 5-second limit in the browser.
hint: Every such stretch grows outwards from a centre, which is either one letter or the gap between two. Grow from each of the $2n - 1$ centres while the two ends agree, and count the stretches whose length has reached `k`.

examples.note: `'aba'` grows from the letter `b`, while `'aa'` and `'baab'` grow from the gap between the two `a`s.
`'zzz'` appears at two positions and counts twice, and `'zzzz'` makes 3.

tests.call: long_mirrors(''.join('ab'[(i * i) % 7 % 2] for i in range(300)), 6)

how: Submit runs 13 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value. Unlike a count of every stretch that reads the same both ways, the floor `k` decides which stretches count as each centre grows.
notes: Every stretch that reads the same both ways grows outwards from one letter or from the gap between two.
Stretches of even length grow from a gap, so growing from letters alone misses `'aa'` and `'baab'`.
There are $2n - 1$ centres and each grows at most $n / 2$ times, so the work is $O(n^2)$.

planted.slip: Counting lengths above `k` leaves out the stretches of length exactly `k`.
Growing only from letters misses every stretch of even length.
Counting distinct stretches merges equal stretches found at different positions.
